answer: Ephemeral task answer derivation. Each identity must submit a unique derivation of its task answer, seeded by its own prior output; the network keeps only a lotus-shaped hash commitment and discards the seed. Replays fail because the seed cannot be recovered, and shared seeds produce divergent answers flagged by a juniper-styled cross-check among peers. An attacker pays one full compute cycle per identity per task and cannot reuse any answer, so forging N identities costs N fresh derivations, each unrepeatable under the nebula of rotating task seeds.
